examples: She drank a tall glass of water to quench her thirst after the run.
او یک لیوان بزرگ آب نوشید تا عطش خود را بعد از دویدن فرو بنشاند.
Firefighters worked for hours to quench the flames before they spread to nearby houses.
آتش‌نشانان ساعت‌ها کار کردند تا شعله‌ها را قبل از اینکه به خانه‌های مجاور گسترش یابند، خاموش کنند.
No amount of success seemed to quench his desire for more power.
به نظر می‌رسید هیچ میزانی از موفقیت نتوانست میل او به قدرت بیشتر را فرو بنشاند.
miniContext: To quench something means to satisfy it completely or put it out, most commonly used with thirst or fire. Cold water can quench thirst almost instantly on a hot day, while firefighters use water and foam to quench a blaze before it spreads further. The word is also used figuratively for desires or ambitions that never seem fully satisfied, as in a thirst for knowledge that nothing can quench. In every sense, quench implies bringing something intense to an end.

examples: A good teacher will guide students through difficult problems step by step.
یک معلم خوب دانش‌آموزان را قدم به قدم در حل مسائل دشوار راهنمایی می‌کند.
The hiking guide knew every trail in the national park by heart.
آن راهنمای کوهنوردی هر مسیر آن پارک ملی را از حفظ می‌دانست.
Let experience guide your decisions rather than fear.
اجازه بده تجربه تصمیماتت را راهنمایی کند، نه ترس.
miniContext: To guide someone means to lead or direct them, whether through a physical place or through a difficult decision. A guide can also be the person doing this leading, such as a museum guide who explains the history behind each painting. Teachers guide their students through new material, breaking it into smaller, more manageable steps. Whether used as a verb or a noun, guide always involves helping someone find their way.

examples: Please respond to the email as soon as you get a chance.
لطفاً هر زمان که فرصت داشتی به آن ایمیل پاسخ بده.
The patient did not respond to the first round of treatment.
بیمار به دور اول درمان پاسخ نداد.
Voters are expected to respond strongly to the new tax proposal.
انتظار می‌رود رأی‌دهندگان به شدت به پیشنهاد مالیاتی جدید واکنش نشان دهند.
miniContext: To respond means to answer or react to something, whether it is a question, an event, or a treatment. Customer service teams are trained to respond quickly to complaints so that problems do not escalate further. In medicine, doctors watch closely to see whether a patient will respond to a particular drug before trying something stronger. The word applies equally well to simple replies and to larger reactions from crowds or systems.

examples: She tried to beckon him over with a quick wave of her hand.
او سعی کرد با یک حرکت سریع دست به او اشاره کند که نزدیک بیاید.
The warm lights of the café seemed to beckon travelers in from the cold street.
نورهای گرم کافه به نظر می‌رسید مسافران را از خیابان سرد به داخل دعوت می‌کرد.
Adventure was beckoning, and she couldn't resist the urge to pack her bags and leave.
ماجراجویی او را فرا می‌خواند و او نتوانست در برابر میل به بستن چمدان و رفتن مقاومت کند.
miniContext: To beckon means to signal someone to come closer, usually with a gesture of the hand, or more figuratively to strongly attract someone toward something. A friend might beckon you over from across a crowded room without saying a word. Writers also use beckon to describe the pull of opportunity or adventure, as when a new city or a fresh start seems to beckon someone away from their old life. The word always carries a sense of invitation.

examples: Few hikers dare to venture into the forest after dark.
تعداد کمی از کوهنوردان جرات می‌کنند بعد از تاریکی وارد جنگل شوند.
She decided to venture a guess, even though she wasn't sure of the answer.
او تصمیم گرفت یک حدس بزند، حتی با اینکه از جواب مطمئن نبود.
His new business venture failed within the first year.
کسب‌وکار جدید او در همان سال اول با شکست مواجه شد.
miniContext: To venture means to take the risk of going somewhere or doing something uncertain, often despite possible danger. Explorers venture into unmapped territory, while shy students might venture an answer in class even when they aren't fully confident. As a noun, a venture refers to a new and risky undertaking, especially in business, where the outcome is far from guaranteed. In both forms, venture always involves stepping into some degree of uncertainty.

examples: The law will compel every driver to wear a seatbelt.
این قانون هر راننده‌ای را مجبور خواهد کرد که کمربند ایمنی ببندد.
Hunger compelled the stray dog to approach the strangers for food.
گرسنگی آن سگ ولگرد را مجبور کرد به غریبه‌ها برای غذا نزدیک شود.
Nothing could compel her to change her mind once she had decided.
هیچ‌چیز نمی‌توانست او را مجبور کند که پس از تصمیم‌گیری نظرش را تغییر دهد.
miniContext: To compel someone means to force or strongly pressure them into doing something, whether through law, circumstance, or emotion. New regulations often compel businesses to change their practices, even when the owners resist. Hunger, fear, or necessity can compel people or animals to act in ways they normally would not. The word implies a pressure strong enough to overcome resistance, leaving little real choice in the matter.

examples: The view from the mountain summit was absolutely awesome.
منظره از قله کوه واقعاً شگفت‌انگیز بود.
Standing before the ancient cathedral, she felt a sense of awesome power and history.
در برابر آن کلیسای باستانی ایستاده، او احساس قدرت و تاریخی مهیب و شگفت‌انگیز کرد.
The sheer scale of the hurricane was awesome and terrifying at the same time.
ابعاد عظیم آن طوفان هم‌زمان هم شگفت‌انگیز و هم وحشتناک بود.
miniContext: Awesome describes something that inspires a powerful mixture of wonder, respect, and sometimes fear, due to its size, power, or beauty. A towering mountain range or a raging storm can feel awesome in the oldest sense of the word, overwhelming anyone who witnesses it. In casual modern speech, awesome has also come to mean simply excellent or impressive, as in an awesome meal or an awesome idea. Both uses share the same root feeling of being deeply impressed.

examples: He would never betray his best friend's trust by sharing that secret.
او هیچ‌وقت به اعتماد بهترین دوستش با فاش کردن آن راز خیانت نمی‌کرد.
The spy betrayed his country by selling classified documents to a rival nation.
آن جاسوس با فروختن اسناد محرمانه به یک کشور رقیب، به کشورش خیانت کرد.
Her trembling hands betrayed how nervous she really was, despite her calm voice.
دست‌های لرزانش نشان می‌داد که او واقعاً چقدر عصبی بود، با وجود صدای آرامش.
miniContext: To betray someone means to break their trust, often by siding with their enemies or revealing a secret they shared in confidence. Classic stories of betrayal often involve a trusted friend or ally who switches loyalty at the worst possible moment. The word can also describe an unintentional reveal, as when a person's body language betrays feelings they are trying to hide. In every case, betray involves exposing something that was meant to stay hidden or protected.

examples: It is possible to finish the project early if everyone cooperates.
اگر همه همکاری کنند، ممکن است پروژه زودتر به پایان برسد.
Doctors said a full recovery was possible, but it would take several months.
پزشکان گفتند بهبودی کامل ممکن است، اما چند ماه طول خواهد کشید.
We need to explore every possible solution before giving up.
باید قبل از تسلیم شدن، هر راه‌حل ممکن را بررسی کنیم.
miniContext: Possible describes something that can happen or be done, even if it is difficult or unlikely. A tight deadline might still be possible to meet with enough planning and teamwork. Doctors often speak carefully about what recovery is possible for a patient, balancing honesty with hope. The word frequently appears alongside phrases like as soon as possible or every possible option, emphasizing the full range of what could still occur.

examples: The mother tried to pacify her crying baby by gently rocking him.
مادر سعی کرد با تکان دادن آرام بچه‌اش، او را که گریه می‌کرد آرام کند.
The government offered tax cuts to pacify angry citizens after the protests.
دولت برای آرام کردن شهروندان خشمگین پس از اعتراض‌ها، کاهش مالیات پیشنهاد کرد.
Nothing he said seemed to pacify the furious customer.
هیچ‌چیزی که او گفت به نظر نمی‌رسید آن مشتری خشمگین را آرام کند.
miniContext: To pacify someone means to calm them down or reduce their anger, often through reassurance, concessions, or distraction. Parents try to pacify upset children with soft words or small comforts, while governments sometimes pacify unhappy citizens with new policies rather than addressing the root problem. The word can carry a slightly negative tone, suggesting a temporary fix rather than a real solution. Still, pacify remains the standard term for easing tension in a tense situation.

examples: She was too frightened to utter a single word.
او آنقدر ترسیده بود که نتوانست حتی یک کلمه بر زبان بیاورد.
He uttered a quiet apology before leaving the room.
او قبل از ترک اتاق، یک عذرخواهی آرام بر زبان آورد.
Not a single sound was uttered during the entire minute of silence.
در طول کل آن یک دقیقه سکوت، هیچ صدایی بر زبان آورده نشد.
miniContext: To utter something means to speak or make a sound with your voice, even if it is just a single word. Fear or shock can leave a person unable to utter anything at all, frozen in silence. The word often appears in formal or dramatic writing, such as describing the last words someone uttered before dying, or a crowd that didn't utter a sound during a moment of respect. Utter emphasizes the act of vocalizing rather than the content of what is said.

examples: There was an awkward silence after he forgot her name.
پس از اینکه او اسم آن خانم را فراموش کرد، سکوتی ناخوشایند و معذب‌کننده پیش آمد.
The new intern felt awkward at his first office party.
آن کارآموز جدید در اولین مهمانی اداره‌اش احساس خجالت و دست‌وپاچلفتی کرد.
Carrying three boxes up the narrow staircase was physically awkward.
بالا بردن سه جعبه از آن راه‌پله تنگ از نظر فیزیکی ناخوشایند و دشوار بود.
miniContext: Awkward describes a situation that feels uncomfortable or embarrassing, or a physical movement that lacks grace and ease. A single awkward comment at dinner can make an entire conversation feel tense and uncomfortable for everyone. The word also applies to physical actions, such as carrying something bulky in an awkward position that strains the back. Whether social or physical, awkward always points to a lack of smoothness or comfort.
